evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Namespace/repository discovery and repository creation MUST use the validated effective capability set; the app MUST NOT assume browser login or PAT implies full management access. If publish is requested and the target repository does not exist, repository creation is guarded by an explicit confirmation showing namespace, repository, and privacy; this confirmation is mandatory and cannot be bypassed by YOLO/autonomy behavior.

items.impact: A capability or repository-existence result can become stale between discovery, confirmation, and creation, leaving authorization failure, duplicate creation, and re-confirmation behavior to builders.
items.statement: The guard correctly binds discovery and creation to validated effective capabilities and makes confirmation autonomy-proof, but it does not define capability freshness, atomic revalidation, already-created races, or the oracle for an invalidated confirmation.
items.title: Repository creation guard lacks TOCTOU semantics

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: doctor.registry.auth is deprecated for DockerHub-specific flows and MUST be treated as an alias of doctor.dockerhub.auth.capability only until old references are removed.

items.impact: Different consumers can remove or retain the alias at different times and produce incompatible doctor identifiers, cached results, or remediation routing.
items.statement: The compatibility direction is explicit, but 'until old references are removed' has no owner, detection rule, telemetry, deadline, version boundary, or acceptance oracle for safe alias removal.
items.title: Deprecated auth alias has no measurable retirement boundary

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Docker action-scope rules keep build-only actions limited to doctor.docker.engine and doctor.docker.buildx unless compose is selected; Run/preview actions require doctor.docker.compose when compose is the selected runtime path and port availability only when a user-facing access URL is expected; Publish requires doctor.dockerhub.auth.capability and doctor.dockerhub.repo.access and must not fail solely because compose validation is irrelevant.

items.impact: Multi-action requests and runtime-path changes can yield inconsistent preflight sets or incorrectly block publish on an unrelated compose failure.
items.statement: Per-action prerequisites are stated, including the publish non-dependency on compose, but the contract does not define how prerequisite sets compose for Build+Run+Publish, how a selected runtime path is frozen, or how irrelevant failed checks are represented rather than propagated.
items.title: Docker preflight rules omit multi-action composition

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Canonical DockerHub/Unraid Doctor rows preserve doctor.docker.buildx, doctor.dockerhub.auth.capability, doctor.dockerhub.repo.access, doctor.unraid.template-repo, and doctor.unraid.ca-profile with their required signals and block/warn/follow-on failure behaviors.

items.impact: Implementations can attach different signals or block/warn behavior to the same check IDs, making preflight and support output non-portable and difficult to test.
items.statement: The required check IDs and behavior classes are preserved, but this unit does not state the check-by-check signal schema, failure-code mapping, block-versus-warn matrix, remediation owner, or observable oracle.
items.title: Doctor rows lack an executable signal and failure matrix

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: docker_auth_result MUST include requested_auth_mode, effective_auth_provider_state, effective_capabilities[], effective_account_identity, last_validation_timestamp, last_validation_host, and degraded_reason?. Evidence/result contract additions record requested mode, effective capability set, account identity, validation timestamp, and degraded reason if any.

items.impact: Account identity, host, and degradation details may be serialized inconsistently, retained too long, or exposed to consumers without redaction and freshness guarantees.
items.statement: The payload minimum is enumerated, but types, nullability beyond degraded_reason?, validation-host normalization, capability ordering, timestamp semantics, schema versioning, redaction, retention, and authorized consumers are unspecified.
items.title: Docker auth result lacks typed privacy and lifecycle rules

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: docker_publish_result MUST include publish_result_id, registry_host, namespace, repository, tags[], digests[], platforms[], and sanitized_logs_path. Evidence/result contract additions record registry host, namespace, repository, pushed tags, digest(s), platform list, and sanitized logs path.

items.impact: A network interruption or partial multi-tag/platform push cannot be represented unambiguously, retried idempotently, or audited without risking inconsistent registry state or sensitive log retention.
items.statement: The minimum identifies publish artifacts, but it omits overall and per-tag/platform status, failure codes, attempt/idempotency identity, partial-success semantics, retry/rollback rules, list-size limits, and the sanitation, access, retention, and missing-file semantics of sanitized_logs_path.
items.title: Docker publish result cannot express partial delivery

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: unraid_template_result MUST include publish_result_id, template_xml_path, template_repo_id, maintainer_slug, commit_status, push_status, ca_profile_state, and review_state. Its enums preserve commit_status values not_attempted, committed, skipped_review_required, skipped_unrelated_changes, failed; push_status values not_attempted, skipped_auto_push_disabled, push_in_progress, completed, failed; review_state values clean and needs_review; and ca_profile_state values existing_user_managed, auto_generated_needs_review, and project_override_active.

items.impact: Consumers can observe impossible combinations such as failed commit with completed push or needs_review with an unguarded push, and cannot determine safe resume or recovery behavior.
items.statement: The payload and enum values are explicit, but valid state combinations, transition triggers, terminality, persistence, crash recovery, concurrent repo mutation handling, and acceptance oracles for each skipped/failed state are not defined.
items.title: Unraid result enums lack a state machine

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: 'DockerHub/Unraid responsibilities are separated: Docker CLI / Buildx performs local runtime, image build, login, and push execution; Docker Hub API is used only for namespace/repository discovery and repository creation when Puppet Master needs app-managed listing/creation behavior; DockerHub is not a storage location for Unraid XML.'

items.impact: The explicit split prevents API scope creep and prevents treating DockerHub as Unraid XML storage.
items.statement: Execution, management API use, and Unraid XML storage authority are separated with a direct negative constraint; this ownership boundary is sufficiently explicit at this unit's level.
items.title: Docker CLI and Hub API ownership is explicitly bounded

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The expanded DockerHub flow detects whether the active project is Docker-related, resolves requested_auth_mode, validates effective_capabilities, allows browser/device login or PAT-based auth with PAT remaining the recommended explicit path, and gates missing-repository creation behind a mandatory confirmation dialog showing namespace, repository name, and privacy that cannot be bypassed by YOLO/autonomy modes.

items.impact: Users may confirm stale namespace/privacy data, receive misleading success or retry states, or face an inaccessible and non-localizable mandatory safety gate.
items.statement: The safety-critical dialog contents and autonomy prohibition are clear, but loading, cancellation, revalidation, repository-created-elsewhere races, permission loss, retry, focus/keyboard behavior, accessible naming, localization, and post-confirmation progress/error states are unspecified.
items.title: Mandatory repository dialog lacks resilient GUI state semantics

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The expanded runtime/publish flow builds with docker buildx build, runs containers for preview/testing and surfaces user-facing access points when available, pushes to DockerHub using the selected namespace/repository/tag set, generates or updates Unraid XML by default unless disabled, and for managed template-repo workflows updates the repo, auto-commits by default, exposes a one-click push UI action, and keeps auto-push disabled by default.

items.impact: Build, preview, registry push, XML mutation, commit, and push can diverge under failures or concurrent edits, while default auto-commit and one-click push may capture unintended changes without a defined recovery boundary.
items.statement: The happy-path sequence and defaults are stated, but transaction boundaries, stage preconditions, unrelated-change detection, commit contents, push confirmation, idempotency, cleanup, network-loss resume, rollback, concurrent repo mutation, and authoritative final-state reporting are absent.
items.title: Build-to-Unraid flow lacks partial-failure and destructive-action controls

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Docker/Unraid evidence/result contract additions preserve docker_auth_result, docker_publish_result, and unraid_template_result summary semantics and retain the final ContractRef overlay to Plans/Containers_Registry_and_Unraid.md, Plans/FinalGUISpec.md, Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md, PolicyRule:no_secrets_in_storage, and SchemaID:evidence.schema.json.

items.impact: GUI, orchestrator, registry, policy, and evidence-schema consumers can diverge on payload semantics or secret handling without a detectable authoritative winner.
items.statement: The overlay names all major authorities and consumers, but it does not specify precedence, schema/version compatibility, required propagation, conflict resolution, or a cross-document conformance oracle.
items.title: Evidence overlay names seams without governing them

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: N2-001 is retired to migration-lineage-only compatibility disposition after Phase 2B batch 107 because newtools-S0001 through newtools-S0078 are covered by N2-002 through N2-150 or explicit structural, reference-only, retired, and migration-coverage dispositions. N2-001 no longer carries source_preserving_planunit compile mode and must not own product coverage.

items.impact: The retired bridge is prevented from regaining product authority or compiling implementation work while preserving migration lineage.
items.statement: Retirement, replacement coverage, compile-mode removal, and the prohibition on product ownership are explicit and are reinforced by acceptance criteria, negative constraints, and migration proof references in the reviewed unit.
items.title: Residual source-preserving bridge is explicitly retired

segments.summary: Reviewed N2-140 through N2-146: capability and autonomy guards are directionally strong, while compatibility exit, composed preflight behavior, doctor-row mapping, payload typing/privacy, partial publish status, and Unraid state transitions remain under-specified.

Reviewed N2-147 through N2-150: the CLI/API ownership split is explicit, but the safety-dialog lifecycle, compound destructive publish workflow, and cross-document evidence overlay need normative failure, synchronization, and conformance contracts.

Reviewed the complete retired N2-001 bridge, its exhaustive successor dependencies, acceptance criteria, negative constraints, proof references, migration coverage, and the following deferred-action addendum lines; the bridge's lineage-only boundary is explicit and non-buildable.

cross_document_questions: Which referenced document is authoritative when Docker and Unraid result semantics conflict, and what versioned conformance check detects drift?
Which owner defines the executable Doctor check signal-to-failure matrix and alias-retirement completion oracle?
Where are partial-failure, idempotency, and recovery semantics for the build, registry push, XML update, commit, and repo-push sequence owned?
research_queries: Docker registry multi-platform push partial failure idempotency digest reconciliation
OAuth device flow capability freshness and repository creation TOCTOU mitigation
safe Git auto-commit and one-click push UX for repositories with unrelated concurrent changes
